requirements: Reproduce the core contributions of 'Calibrated Speculative Decoding: Frequency-Guided Candidate Selection for Efficient Inference' — the training-free CSD framework with Online Correction Memory (OCM) and Semantic Consistency Gating (SCG), across Llama-3 and Qwen-2.5 model pairs, matching the reported acceptance rates, throughput speedups (up to 2.33×), and accuracy on GSM8K, MATH500, HumanEval, CNN/DM, IFEval, and RULER.

sub_tasks.requirements: Establish the hardware and software stack: 8× NVIDIA H20 GPU node, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, lm-evaluation-harness, and the single-batch inference harness that CSD is measured under (Section 5.1).
Provision the GPU compute node and confirm it meets the paper's hardware specification.

Code has been implemented to detect and report the local GPU inventory (e.g., via `nvidia-smi` or `torch.cuda.device_count()`), and the environment provisioning script verifies that at least 8 NVIDIA H20 GPUs are visible to CUDA before starting any CSD run.

verification.spec: Locate the environment provisioning script (e.g., setup.sh, provision.py, or reproduce.sh preamble). Grep for calls to `nvidia-smi` or `torch.cuda.device_count()` and assert the script fails/exits non-zero when fewer than 8 GPUs are visible. Run the script inside a shell where CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES is limited to 0-6 (7 GPUs) and confirm it aborts; run again with all 8 visible and confirm it proceeds.

verification.spec: Import the target-model loader helper. Instantiate the 70B/72B target model via the code path used in evaluation and inspect `model.hf_device_map` (or equivalent). Assert that exactly 2 distinct CUDA device ids appear across the module placements for the target model, and that the draft-model loader places its weights on a different device id.

verification.spec: Invoke the evaluation entrypoint in 'final' mode and inspect the sampling config passed to model.generate; assert temperature == 0 (or do_sample=False). sub_tasks.requirements: Implement timing/throughput measurement infrastructure that produces the tokens/s, speedup, and latency-breakdown numbers reported in Tables 1–5 and Figure 4.

Code has been implemented that measures throughput as (accepted output tokens) / (wall-clock generation seconds) per request, using `torch.cuda.synchronize()` around each generate call so tokens/s numbers reported by the harness are steady-state and not skewed by asynchronous CUDA kernels.

verification.spec: Grep the CSD engine / harness wrapper source for `torch.cuda.synchronize()` calls surrounding each generate call and confirm the throughput calculation divides accepted-output-token count by the wall-clock delta measured between the syncs. Run a small generation and assert reported tokens/s is finite and positive.

verification.spec: Run the profiling harness on a short generation and confirm the output log contains four labeled per-component latency numbers: draft-model forward, target-model forward, CSD algorithmic overhead, and system overhead. Assert they sum to within a few percent of the measured total request latency, matching Figure 4's breakdown categories.

sub_tasks.requirements: Implement Phase 2 Online Evolution: the Dynamic Update rule that increments T for every verified divergence encountered at inference time (Algorithm 1 line 18), running with zero online training overhead.

sub_tasks.requirements: The online Dynamic Update path introduces no additional model forward or backward passes beyond those already required by standard speculative decoding — a unit-level check confirms that per-step model FLOPs/forward-call counts under CSD (excluding SCG logit reads) are unchanged from SpecDecode.

Run one iteration of standard SpecDecode and one iteration of CSD (with SCG stubbed to constant, forcing update-memory path) on identical inputs with identical seeds. Run CSD on MATH500 with Llama-3-70B target + Llama-3.2-1B draft at gamma=6, tau=0.01, lambda=6, greedy (T=0). Also run standard SpecDecode with matching gamma. sub_tasks.requirements: Implement the Candidate Proposal gating rule: OCM proposes a rescue candidate only when the observed frequency of the divergence pair meets the threshold λ, i.e., is_freq ← (T[(x̃_i, t*)] ≥ λ) as in Algorithm 1 line 16.
Code has been implemented that exposes a boolean predicate is_freq(x̃_i, t*) := (T[(x̃_i, t*)] ≥ λ) computed inside the CSD rejection branch prior to any rescue decision.

verification.spec: Locate the CSD rescue code path. Verify that inside the rejection branch, before the SCG check, a callable such as `is_freq(draft_id, target_id)` is invoked returning bool. Confirm via tracing that is_freq is evaluated prior to the rescue decision.

sub_tasks.requirements: Implement Semantic Consistency Gating (SCG): the logit-space admissibility check z_i(x̃) − z_i(t*) ≥ ln(τ) (Eq. 3), the tunable gating threshold τ, its softmax-free / temperature-invariant properties, and correct integration with the rejection-sampling correction token t* on Algorithm 1 line 17.
Implement the semantic admissibility check in the logit space as z_i(x̃_i) − z_i(t*) ≥ ln(τ) (Eq. 3), including softmax-free and temperature-invariance properties.

Code has been implemented for a `semantic_admissibility(logits, draft_id, target_id, tau)` function (or equivalent) that returns True iff z_i(draft_id) − z_i(target_id) ≥ ln(tau), taking raw target-model logits as input.

verification.spec: Import the semantic_admissibility function. Construct a logits tensor of shape [vocab] with z[3]=2.0, z[7]=1.0. With tau=0.1 (ln tau = -2.303): check semantic_admissibility(logits, draft_id=3, target_id=7, tau=0.1) returns True since 2-1=1 >= -2.303. Then with z[3]=-5, z[7]=1 the diff is -6 < -2.303, expect False. Test at least 3 numeric cases including boundary equality.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the SCG check operates directly on raw logits without ever calling softmax, log_softmax, or normalizing over the vocabulary; the implementation must not compute p_i(x̃_i)/p_i(t*) as an explicit ratio of probabilities.

verification.spec: Static-analyze the SCG module: grep the source for calls to `softmax`, `log_softmax`, `.softmax`, `F.softmax`, `torch.softmax`, `normalize`, or an explicit probability division `p_i / p_t`. Assert none appear inside the admissibility function. Optionally monkey-patch torch.nn.functional.softmax to raise, invoke the gate, and assert it still returns without raising.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the admissibility decision is invariant to sampling temperature T: dividing all input logits by any T>0 (equivalent to the temperature scaling applied elsewhere in the pipeline) does not change the boolean output of the gate — a deterministic unit test verifies this on synthetic logits.

verification.spec: Generate a random logits vector L of size 32000. For draft_id=100, target_id=200, tau=0.01, compute gate(L) and gate(L/T) for T in {0.6, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0}. verification.spec: Construct a synthetic logit vector where z_i(x̃_i) - z_i(t*) exactly equals ln(τ) for τ=0.01. Call the SCG admissibility function and assert it returns True. Then subtract a small ε=1e-6 from z_i(x̃_i) and re-invoke; assert it returns False. Repeat for τ=0.5.

verification.spec: For 50 random logits vectors (vocab 32000) and 50 random (draft_id, target_id) pairs at tau=0.01, compute (a) the logit-space gate output and (b) reference boolean p[draft]/p[target] >= tau where p = softmax(logits). sub_tasks.requirements: Hardware / library platforms used in the paper

Code has been implemented and run such that the environment provides a working CUDA + PyTorch + Hugging Face Transformers stack (per Paszke et al. 2019 / Wolf et al. 2020) sufficient to load a 70B-class model across 2 GPUs and perform inference with speculative decoding.

verification.spec: Assert that `import torch; import transformers` succeeds; assert torch.cuda.is_available() and torch.cuda.device_count() >= 2; assert transformers.__version__ is set; assert a small Llama-3 model can be loaded and forward-passed.

sub_tasks.requirements: Environment pins Hugging Face Transformers to a specific version compatible with Llama-3 and Qwen-2.5 model loading (per Wolf et al., 2020 citation in Implementation Details).

verification.spec: Import transformers; assert transformers.__version__ is pinned in requirements.txt/pyproject.toml (not floating); assert version >= 4.40 to support Llama-3 and Qwen-2.5 architectures.

sub_tasks.requirements: Environment pins lm-evaluation-harness to a specific commit/version used for GSM8K, MATH500, HumanEval, and CNN/DailyMail evaluations.

verification.spec: Assert repository declares a pinned lm-evaluation-harness commit hash or version tag in reproduce.sh or requirements; import lm_eval and confirm the module loads with expected task registrations for gsm8k, hendrycks_math, humaneval, cnn_dailymail.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run on an NVIDIA H20 GPU node with ≥8 GPUs where 2 GPUs are allocated per inference session to load the 70B/72B target model.

verification.spec: Query torch.cuda.device_count() >= 2 and confirm target model is loaded with device_map spanning exactly 2 GPUs; on H100 (fallback), verify the loader accepts multi-GPU sharding with tensor parallelism = 2.

sub_tasks.requirements: Single-batch (batch_size=1) inference setting is enforced globally in all evaluation entry points.

verification.spec: Invoke the evaluation runner and inspect the batching config; assert batch_size == 1 for all four evaluation tasks; also assert the generation loop rejects batched inputs of size > 1.

sub_tasks.requirements: Greedy decoding (T=0) is used for all final performance/throughput evaluation, and T=0.6 is used during CSD calibration.

verification.spec: Inspect config: eval-time temperature must equal 0.0 (or do_sample=False); calibration script sets temperature=0.6. Run a short greedy pass and confirm identical outputs across two seeds.

sub_tasks.requirements: Method components (from critique splits and additions)
Code has been implemented and run such that Figure 1 (Overview of Calibrated Speculative Decoding) is reproduced or a functional equivalent diagram is generated illustrating the standard vs CSD flow.

verification.spec: Assert that a figure file (e.g., results/figure1_overview.png/pdf) exists in the reproduction results directory describing the standard SD vs CSD comparison workflow.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that the illustrative example '2 × 5 = 10' (draft) vs '2 * 5 = 10' (target) from Figure 1 is captured as a canonical example of trivial lexical divergence handled by CSD, with a unit test showing the rescue mechanism accepts the draft.

verification.spec: Construct a mock draft/target pair where draft emits '×' and target prefers '*' at position i. Run CSD's rescue mechanism (OCM + SCG with paper's thresholds tau=0.01, lambda=6) with sufficient prior frequency and assert the draft token is accepted, so subsequent '5=10' tokens survive.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that Eq. 1 (autoregressive draft sampling x_i ~ q(·|x, x_<i) from Mq) is implemented as a callable function in the CSD source.

verification.spec: Import the CSD package and assert a draft-sampling function exists that takes a draft model Mq, prefix x, and steps gamma, and returns gamma sampled tokens. Verify shape and dtype.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that Eq. 2 (acceptance probability alpha_i = min(1, p_i(x_i)/q_i(x_i)) for rejection sampling) is implemented in the standard speculative decoding verifier.

verification.spec: Unit test the acceptance-probability function: for known scalar values (p=0.4, q=0.8) assert alpha=0.5; for p>=q assert alpha=1.0. Also test rejection resampling from norm(max(0, p-q)).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that Eq. 3 (Semantic Consistency Gating in logit space, checking z_i(x_tilde_i) - z_i(t*) >= log(tau)) is implemented as the SCG admissibility check.

verification.spec: Unit test the SCG function: for logits z where z[x_tilde]=5.0, z[t*]=7.0, tau=0.01, assert the check passes (diff=-2.0 >= log(0.01)~=-4.605); for a case where diff=-6.0 assert it fails. Verify temperature invariance.

sub_tasks.requirements: Method implements draft phase (Algorithm 1 lines 1-4): γ candidate tokens are sampled autoregressively from the draft model Mq at temperature T.

verification.spec: Instrument the draft loop; assert exactly γ forward passes on Mq with the specified temperature, and that q_i(·) distributions are recorded for use in acceptance test. Test with γ=6 on a small prefix.

sub_tasks.requirements: Method implements parallel verification (Algorithm 1 line 5): a single forward pass of Mp on the drafted sequence produces target probabilities p_{1:γ+1}.

verification.spec: Instrument Mp calls; assert exactly ONE forward pass on Mp per speculative iteration; confirm the returned probability tensor has length γ+1 in the sequence dimension.

sub_tasks.requirements: Method implements the standard rejection acceptance test (Algorithm 1 lines 7-11): draw r ~ U[0,1], accept x̃_i iff r ≤ min(1, p_i(x̃_i)/q_i(x̃_i)).

verification.spec: Unit test: feed synthetic p_i, q_i with known ratios and a fixed seed; assert acceptance decisions match reference min(1, p/q) formula for both accept (r<α) and reject (r>α) cases.

sub_tasks.requirements: Method implements correction resampling on rejection (Algorithm 1 lines 13-14): t* ~ norm(max(0, p_i - q_i)).

verification.spec: Unit test: build synthetic p, q vectors where p-q has known positive/negative entries; call the resampler; assert output support only over indices where p>q and probabilities sum to 1.

sub_tasks.requirements: CSD rescue path (Algorithm 1 lines 15-20) requires BOTH is_freq (T[(x̃_i,t*)] ≥ λ) AND is_safe (semantic gating) to be true; UPDATEMEMORY(T, x̃_i, t*) is called on every rejection regardless of rescue outcome.

verification.spec: Unit tests: (a) is_freq=True, is_safe=False → not rescued; (b) is_freq=False, is_safe=True → not rescued; (c) both True → rescued (n increments); (d) verify UPDATEMEMORY is called in all three cases (side-effect on T counter).

sub_tasks.requirements: Method implements failed-rescue return (Algorithm 1 line 22): when rescue conditions fail, return prefix ⊕ [x̃_1, ..., x̃_n, t*] where t* is the resampled correction.

verification.spec: Force a rejection at position n<γ with rescue disabled; assert returned sequence equals prefix + accepted-drafts[:n] + [t*] (length = |prefix|+n+1); no additional tokens are appended.

sub_tasks.requirements: Method implements all-accepted bonus-token branch (Algorithm 1 lines 26-27): when all γ drafts are accepted, sample one extra token t ~ p_{γ+1}(x) from the target and append.

verification.spec: Construct a scenario where p_i(x̃_i) >= q_i(x̃_i) for all i (guaranteed acceptance); run one CSD step; assert output length equals |prefix|+γ+1 and that the (γ+1)-th token is drawn from the target's p_{γ+1} distribution.
